activities.anchor: This lesson maps the designs, the flagship
activities.caption: scrub the invention dates and the designed scripts
activities.name: wswInventionTimeline

events.title: Mesopotamia: tokens to cuneiform
events.text: Clay accounting counters stiffen into pictographs, then stylise under the stylus — the earliest pristine case.

events.title: China: oracle-bone script
events.text: The same pictograph-to-character path, taken separately.

events.title: Mesoamerica: Mayan glyphs
events.text: Full language recorded by the first millennium BCE — the third pristine case (Egypt a probable fourth).

events.title: Hangul, engineered on purpose
events.text: King Sejong's featural alphabet — letter shapes drawn from the mouth's articulators, promulgated to raise commoner literacy.

events.title: Turkey re-scripts onto Latin
events.text: Writing-system choice as language policy — past literature cut off from new readers.

activities.caption: pair each design with the unit it writes
activities.name: wswDesignMatch

config.prompt: Each design is a bet on what language is made of — pair the design with its unit:

pairs.right: a symbol per phoneme — some 20–40 signs cover any word
consonants written, short vowels mostly unwritten — k-t-b gives kitāb and kātib
one symbol per syllable or mora — about 100 signs in Japanese
a character per morpheme — legible across three millennia of sound change

config.why: Phonemes are abstractions nothing in the sound stream isolates, so alphabets take explicit teaching; abjads economise for consonantal-root morphology; kana stay learnable because the mapping is small and closed; hanzi stay legible across dialects and centuries.

activities.caption: find the line the picture-myth would love
activities.name: wswHanziSpot

config.prompt: One line of this summary is the picture-myth speaking — click it:
lines: True pictographs — drawings of things — are a small minority of characters.
The large majority are phono-semantic compounds.
A semantic radical names the associated domain (氵 in 河).
Characters are little pictures of what they name, so learning them is drawing-learning.
A phonetic component cues the sound (可 kě).
config.correction: Pattern-learning, not picture-learning: radical plus phonetic component — a partially sound-based system hiding inside a logography.
config.why: The sound cues let readers often pronounce characters never seen — nothing a pure picture-system could do.

activities.anchor: learned in a weekend with mnemonics
activities.caption: call the sign count of the weekend win
activities.name: wswKanaEstimate

config.prompt: Hiragana and katakana together: about how many basic signs must a learner master?
config.why: 46 hiragana for native grammar plus 46 katakana for loanwords and emphasis — a small, closed mapping, which is why a couple of days of mnemonics delivers the learner's first unambiguous win in Japanese.
config.context: Compare the only long game: roughly 50,000 Han characters exist, about 3,000 cover ordinary reading, and educated readers command 4,000–8,000.

activities.anchor: four systems interleaved, parsed without pause
activities.caption: file each job to the sub-system that does it
activities.name: wswKanjiBuckets

config.prompt: The jobs inside a single line of Japanese — file each one:

items.label: the morpheme core of a verb

config.why: Every job read in one sweep — and Korean shows the reverse migration: Hanja largely replaced by Sejong's engineered blocks, consonant letters drawn from the mouth's articulators (ㅁ closed lips, ㅅ the tooth ridge) and packed into syllable blocks.

activities.anchor: readers of Chinese make shorter saccades over denser information
activities.caption: call the constant reading bandwidth
activities.name: wswBitsEstimate

config.prompt: Pelli's invariance: throughput at the page is roughly constant across every writing system. How many bits per second does a reader deliver?
config.why: About 40–50 bits per second regardless of script: alphabets trade more symbols for shorter words; logographies trade fewer, denser units — the brain converges on the same bandwidth, so no design is superior.
config.context: Depth still shows elsewhere: transparent orthographies are learned faster, and dyslexia manifests as phonological assembly failure in English but more visual-orthographic trouble in Chinese.

activities.anchor: Writing's evolution follows a logic worth knowing
activities.caption: rebuild the deep story, stage by stage
activities.name: wswEvolutionOrder

config.prompt: Every learner's script recapitulates the deep story — order the stages:
items: Clay accounting tokens for sheep, grain and jars (Schmandt-Besserat)
Tokens stiffen into pictographs — the sheep token drawn on the tablet
The rebus principle: draw the reed (gi), spell the syllable gi in any word
Cuneiform stylises the pictures; oracle-bone script follows the same path
Semitic scribes keep only consonants; Greek borrowers add vowels — the final compression
config.why: The rebus unlocks syllables from pictures and makes full language writable; the Greek vowel move is the one genuine conceptual leap — phonemes are never pronounced alone, so symbolising them took a second-order insight, made once and inherited by Latin, Cyrillic, Armenian and dozens more.

activities.anchor: they carry identity the way flags do
activities.caption: pair each case with its script arrangement
activities.name: wswDigraphiaMatch

config.prompt: One language, two scripts, or two varieties — pair each case with its arrangement:

pairs.right: substantially one spoken language (Hindustani) in Devanagari and Nastaliq — the literatures pull the registers apart
Cyrillic and Latin run officially in parallel
two standardised written varieties, Bokmål and Nynorsk, from different dialect bases
script revival as nation- and community-building

config.why: States have re-scripted populations deliberately (Turkey 1928, the Central Asian Latinisations, Soviet Cyrillicisations) — learn a script and you join a historically positioned community of readers.
